items.grounds: Re-derived both ways. Bytes: the row's opening verse is exactly בַּיּ֖וֹם הַה֑וּא כֶּ֥רֶם חֶ֖מֶד עַנּוּ לָֽהּ (oshb:Isa.27.2, byte tier — the entire verse) and its closing verse ends שָׁל֖וֹם יַֽעֲשֶׂה לִּֽי (oshb:Isa.27.5, byte tier, verse-final); no verse in oshb:Isa.27.2-Isa.27.5 carries any quotation character. The quotation apparatus is WEB-side only: web:Isa.27.2 carries a single opening curly double quote with no closer in its verse, web:Isa.27.3-Isa.27.4 carry none, and web:Isa.27.5 ends with the single closing curly double quote — the finding's punctuation reading is exact. The rationale does carry this as a translation-punctuation boundary offered as 'non-driving corroboration alone': under the marker policy tier-4 translation punctuation is never boundary evidence at any weight, and 'corroboration' is an evidence role — the non-driving label does not license it inside the warrant. Not alone load-bearing: the same sentence grounds the rear edge on the spliced oshb:Isa.27.6 onset, so medium as filed.

Re-derived. The clause 'the book's one instance of a dedicated song-announcement formula' is a universal with no digit-bearing sweep citation anywhere in the rationale and no defined swept object. Re-swept: the consonantal substring שיר stands at 9 verses book-wide (sweep: 9 verses — a blended substring object: the oshb:Isa.3.19 hit token is the necklace noun and the oshb:Isa.53.9 hit token the rich-man noun, exactly as the finding discloses). Byte counterevidence re-collates: אָשִׁ֤ירָה נָּא֙ לִֽידִידִ֔י שִׁירַ֥ת דּוֹדִ֖י (oshb:Isa.5.1, byte tier) is a first-person song announcement introducing the very vineyard song this row cites at web:Isa.5.1-Isa.5.7, and שִׁ֤ירוּ לַֽיהוָה֙ שִׁ֣יר חָדָ֔שׁ (oshb:Isa.42.10, byte tier) is an imperative song summons — beside יוּשַׁ֥ר הַשִּׁיר (oshb:Isa.26.1, byte tier), the 'one instance' claim fails under any byte-operational construal of the object. It backs the construal disclaimer, not the day-formula onset driving the front edge: medium as filed.

Re-derived from bytes. The rear-edge verse reads הַבָּאִים֙ יַשְׁרֵ֣שׁ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב יָצִ֥יץ וּפָרַ֖ח יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Isa.27.6, byte tier): the names stand as third-person subjects of third-person verbs, with no vocative particle and no second-person form anywhere in the verse (form-class argued from the pointed bytes and both renderings; no morphology layer is staged). Inside the row's span the vineyard is carried by third-feminine-singular forms — אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ נֹֽצְרָ֔הּ (oshb:Isa.27.3, byte tier) — and the span's only second-person form is the plural imperative עַנּוּ לָֽהּ (oshb:Isa.27.2, byte tier), addressed to an unnamed audience about the vineyard, not to it. Both halves of the rationale's contrast — 'addressing Jacob and Israel by name' and 'continuing the vineyard's second-person/first-person address' — are byte-false as form-class claims, while the seam itself survives on the referent/scene shift the same spliced bytes carry. Defective warrant ground, not a boundary defect: medium as filed.

Re-derived. The closing sentence asserts the Hebrew frame onset in transliteration only, and boundary_evidence_refs carries web:Isa.27.12 with no oshb:Isa.27.12 — verified against the shipped row. The verse's own bytes open verse-initially with וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא (oshb:Isa.27.12, byte tier), the waw-prefixed long form of the formula — the very bare-vs-long distinction the neighbouring rows argue from, left unstated here. The claim is true in substance, so the defect is the missing mandatory pointed splice, tier label, and oshb ref on a boundary-relevant Hebrew claim, leaving the rear-edge warrant resting on the rendering: medium as filed.

Re-derived. parent_collection is the M2 frame ending at Isa.27.13, rows never straddle a frame seam, and this row spans Isa.27.13-Isa.27.13 — the close at Isa.27.13 is entailed by campaign architecture, and the rationale states the parent-grouping fact twice, the second time expressly as corroboration of the row's own close. Architecture is law, not observation: the clause adds nothing about the textual seam. The genuine rear-edge ground re-derives from bytes: ה֗וֹי (oshb:Isa.28.1, byte tier) opens that verse, the verse-initial woe onset of the fresh series. With that ground standing, the circular clause is a defective warrant element, not a boundary defect: medium as filed.

Re-derived. וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא (oshb:Isa.27.12, byte tier) and וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.27.13, byte tier) are each verse-initial in their own verse, and each run reaches only accent_stripped tier against the other's verse — the two long-form onsets differ in accents alone, exactly as the neighbour row's rejected-alternative records. The shipped pair registers this one seam asymmetrically: the neighbour (span Isa.27.12-Isa.27.12) ships confidence medium with frontier_flag_considered true and weighs the merge rival expressly, while this row ships confidence high with frontier_flag_considered false and grounds its front edge on 'its own repetition of the day-formula' — the shared feature itself — plus the tier-3 setumah recorded at oshb:Isa.27.12 (single-witness). A shared-feature ground cannot be more settled on one side of a seam than the other side registers it; the rear edge (the oshb:Isa.28.1 woe onset at the frame seam) is untouched. Registration incoherence with the span sound: medium as filed.

Re-derived. בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.28.5, byte tier) is verse-initial there, and that same run reaches only accent_stripped tier against oshb:Isa.27.1 and against oshb:Isa.27.2; the three bare verse-initial onsets בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.28.5, byte tier), בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֡וּא (oshb:Isa.27.1, byte tier) and בַּיּ֖וֹם הַה֑וּא (oshb:Isa.27.2, byte tier) are pairwise distinct at byte tier, differing in accents alone. The rejected-alternative's sameness clause names no tier, in a row that tier-labels its other recurrence claims — 'bare' and 'verse-initial' are byte-true, but 'the same ... formula' is false at the byte tier its adjacent splices invoke and true only at accent_stripped tier. The row's crown digits re-derive exactly: the consonantal substring עטרת stands at 4 verses book-wide (sweep: 4 verses — oshb:Isa.28.1, oshb:Isa.28.3, oshb:Isa.28.5, oshb:Isa.62.3), 3 of them in chapter 28. A missing mandatory tier label on a recurrence claim inside the weighed rival, not load-bearing for the kept span: medium as filed.

Re-derived. The rear-edge clause rests on web:Isa.28.14 alone and boundary_evidence_refs carries no oshb:Isa.28.14 — verified against the shipped row. The verse's own bytes open verse-initially with לָכֵ֛ן שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אַנְשֵׁ֣י לָצ֑וֹן (oshb:Isa.28.14, byte tier): the imperative summons with its named addressee is real, so the claim is true in substance but unspliced where pointed splices and tier labels are mandatory for boundary-relevant Hebrew claims. The strongest regional mark is disclosed correctly — PE recorded at oshb:Isa.28.13 in the parashah inventory, cited by the row as petuchah (single-witness), not conflated with SAMEKH — and as tier-3 it cannot carry the edge either. Warrant shortfall on a true rear-edge claim: medium as filed.
